newsitem.title: USA: Quaker sets restructuring, succession plan.
newsitem.headline: Quaker sets restructuring, succession plan.

text.p: Quaker Oats Co said Wednesday it is forming a plan that, when finalized, will include share repurchases and cost reductions programs as well as succession to the post now held by William Smithburg, chairman.
Quaker said it expects to take restructuring charges of $50 million to $100 million pretax before the end of the year.
The company said it is reviewing the sale of non-core businesses and the potential restructuring of certain international operations.

Quaker said Smithburg, who has served as chief executive officer for over 16 years, wanted to formalize an orderly succession plan. It added that the board, at Smithburg's suggestion, formed a committee, which will be chaired by William Weiss, an outside director, to search for successors from both inside and outside the company.
Smithburg, in the interim, will continue to lead the organization and implement the company's refocusing efforts.
The 1996 Quaker annual report listed Smithburg's age as 58.

Commenting on the strategic plan that Quaker is forming, Smithburg said that strong cash flows from core businesses, along with proceeds from divestitures, will allow the company to renew its share repurchase program.

"Quaker has a team working on overhead cost reductions with a goal of reducing costs by $30 million over an 18-month period, in addition to removing or absorbing costs related to the sale of Snapple," Smithburg said in a statement. "This is an ongoing program, designed to create a culture in which Quaker will pursue ways to reduce costs, further increase efficiencies and benefit our customers and shareholders."

Quaker has announced a plan to sell Snapple, which resulted in an after-tax loss for the company of $1.14 billion or $8.39 a share in the first quarter. Earlier, it reported net income for the first quarter, excluding the Snapple loss, of $0.24 a share, up from $0.22 a year ago.
Quaker said it intends to review the divestiture of some small businesses that do not fit into its strategy to build upon grain-based foods and Gatorade sports drink.

"Our strategic portfolio changes are showing impressive results in our core U.S. and Canadian Foods and Gatorade businesses," Smithburg said. "Our leading brands with higher margins in growing categories represent the strongest portfolio of brands in Quaker's history."
He added that the company expects to stimulate its international profitability by concentrating almost exclusively on its Quaker and Gatorade brands, which have good consumer recognition abroad.
